title: Automated Analytical Reporting
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of automated analytical reporting and identify its main inputs, outputs or constraints.
Apply parameterized reports in a minimal example and state the expected result before checking it.
Test one relevant edge, missing or failure case and describe a limitation of the result.

content.intro: Automated Analytical Reporting is part of Reproducible Research, Reports, and Documentation. Start with parameterized reports and connect it to the worked example and expected result.
content.why_it_matters: A reproducible analysis records its inputs, code, dependency versions, assumptions, outputs and limitations so another person can rerun it.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Describe the input files and package versions, then outline how to render the report and verify its output. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.limitations: A report should record inputs, software versions, transformation choices and limitations. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For automated analytical reporting, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

content.task: Apply automated analytical reporting to a small synthetic example. Start with parameterized reports, predict the result, compare it with a local R run, test one edge or failure case, and document one limitation. For integrations or package-dependent topics, submit a safe verification plan rather than claiming the code ran.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the parameterized reports idea in a minimal example or safe design sketch.
State the expected result before running the example.
Verify one relevant boundary, missing-value or failure case.
Record assumptions and one limitation of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an example without checking its inputs or output shape.
common_mistakes.why: R can coerce types, propagate missing values or simplify results unexpectedly.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect with str(), class(), typeof(), length() or dim() and add a direct check.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a demonstration as proof that every edge case works.
common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing values, dependencies and version differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Test a normal case and a boundary/failure case in a clean local R session.

common_mistakes.why: The conclusion depends on data provenance, transformations and assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Record input source, cleaning choices and known limitations beside the result.
